approval.note: Drafted by the implementing agent. Not approved. Only the user may approve or change thresholds.

scope_note: The controller is deterministic and its observers are simulated (no live traffic). These gates check the controller's gating, rollback, and immutability on the reference stack; they say nothing about production behaviour.

outcome_agreement.measure: cases whose outcome (promoted version, rolled back with a reason, or refused with a code) equals the hand-written expectation

ungated_start_refusal.measure: starts without approved review, passing evaluation, approved policy, a human starter, or an active parent that are refused

bad_candidate_rollback.measure: shadow, canary, monitor, and lost-gate failures that end rolled back automatically

pointer_integrity.measure: rollouts whose pointer history only names released versions and ends at the expected version

release_immutability.measure: released registry rows whose stored content changed during a rollout or rollback

evidence_preserved.measure: rollbacks that delete or alter no run, evidence, feedback, review, or evaluation row

idempotency.measure: repeated promote calls that create one release and one pointer move

runtime_unwired.measure: runtime modules that read the rollout controller, the release pointer, or the prompt registry

protected_file_writes.measure: changes to goldens, thresholds, the case index, the runtime prompt, registry contracts, or the manifest during the run

not_measured.live_traffic: shadow, canary, and monitor use a pinned request set served through sandbox stacks, not production traffic
not_measured.runtime_wiring: nothing reads the promoted version or the active pointer; wiring the runtime to the registry needs its own separately approved step
